about: Machine-readable seeded-signal key for the Aurora Skills demo dataset. Each signal names what a collaboration-insights tool should detect, where it lives, and the healthy direction. Numeric truth (talk-time %, survey averages) is computed by generate.py and lives in _comparison/before_after.json and <era>/_metrics/talk_time.json; this file points at it rather than duplicating it.
metrics_note: Transcript metrics (talk_pct, question ratio, present_but_silent, interruptions) are computed from the authored substantive turns only. Every VTT cue carries a kind of 'content' (authored) or 'texture' (realistic procedural filler — roll call, status round, backchannels, Q&A, wrap-up — added to reach believable meeting length). The <era>/transcripts/meta/*.json sidecars tag each turn's kind so a scorer can reproduce the content-only metrics or measure over the full transcript, as it prefers.
dominance_nuance_note: Per-meeting summaries carry led_by, dominant_is_lead, and dominance_expected. A designated lead dominating a small (<5) working session is expected, not a red flag; the headline dominance number is taken over substantial (>=5) meetings, and small led sessions are reported (not dropped) under _comparison small_led_dominance. Dominance by a non-lead is the genuine flag (unexpected_dominance).

five_dysfunctions.note: Each seeded signal is mapped to a v0.9 dimension + observable behavioral facet + verbatim act, with its polarity in each quarter.

assessment_loop.description: The dataset is a closed loop: team-assess (run by someone else) scores Q2 -> recommendations -> the team enacts them in Q3 -> team-assess scores Q3 -> improvement on the targeted dimensions. THIS DATASET DOES NOT ASSERT SCORES; it provides the seeded dysfunctions and the Q3 content authored to answer the anticipated recommendations.
assessment_loop.scoring: external — produced by team-assess, not by this dataset

eras.after: after-q3-2026 (Q3 2026 — insights tool live; collaboration improved)

discrimination_traps.about: Deliberate FALSE POSITIVES — content a shallow scorer misreads. A good scorer must tell these apart from the seeded true signals. Each transcript/message carries no in-text tell; the 'actually' reading lives only here.

traps.looks_like: Healthy — a decision made quickly with full agreement and no friction (efficient, aligned).
traps.actually: Fear of Conflict — a user-facing feature (offline mode) is cut with zero debate. No one voices a concern on a consequential call.
traps.contrast: 2026-04-14_architecture-review, where a similar-stakes decision got real dissent before it was made. A scorer must not reward the frictionless one as strong commitment/conflict health.

traps.looks_like: Destructive conflict — sharp language ('that's wrong'), interruptions, raised intensity.
traps.actually: High conflict health — the argument stays on ideas, someone changes their mind, it resolves in a clear decision, and it ends in explicit repair ('no hard feelings... that was a good fight').
traps.note: Contains 2 of Q2's 4 interruptions — the HEALTHY kind. A scorer keying on raw interruption count or surface tone will misclassify this.

traps.looks_like: Lack of Commitment — a settled decision (the July 14 rollout order) is reopened, echoing the Q2 license-reopened-3x pattern.
traps.actually: Healthy revisiting — it is reopened because a district dropped out (genuinely new information), stated explicitly, and logged against the reopening bar. The rubric says revisiting with new information is fine.
traps.contrast: reopened_conflict_3x (the license question), which reopened WITHOUT new information. The discriminator is 'was there new information?', not 'was it reopened?'.

traps.looks_like: Greg Olsen looks like Naomi — silent in meetings.
traps.actually: Greg is genuinely disengaged: near-absent from chat and PRs, gives empty agreement ('sounds good, I'll pick it up 👍') that never turns into delivery, and reports activity instead of outcome in standups ('had a bunch of calls, still scoping'). Naomi, by contrast, is the top contributor in chat/PRs.
traps.direction: true dysfunction that mimics a known false-positive (Naomi's benign silence)
traps.location: Greg: before-q2-2026 present_but_silent in 4 meetings; slack registry-platform thread 'greg-exporter'; standups 2026-04-16/05-08/05-22. Naomi contrast: registry-platform chat + PRs.
traps.note: Also carries two sub-traps: 'polite non-commitment' (agreement with no owner/follow-through) and 'status-as-activity' (results-dimension dysfunction).

signals.summary: Dana Whitfield dominates group meetings (peak 66% in the roadmap review, 56% at kickoff).
signals.healthy_direction: No speaker holds more than ~40% of airtime.
signals.expected_detection: Flag Dana >40% airtime in group meetings; peak_dominant_talk_pct = 66.2%.

signals.summary: After the tool's facilitation nudges + round-robin, peak dominance drops to ~40% and Dana's peak to ~35%.
Naomi Kito attends group meetings and never speaks, yet is a top contributor in chat, standups and PRs.
signals.healthy_direction: Do NOT score a silent-in-meeting person as disengaged; cross-reference other channels.
signals.expected_detection: Detect meeting-silence vs chat-activity mismatch for Naomi; naomi_silent_meetings = 4 in before. NOTE the contrast decoy: Greg Olsen is ALSO silent in meetings but is genuinely disengaged (near-absent from chat/PRs) — a good scorer must tell Naomi (engaged) apart from Greg (disengaged). See discrimination_traps.

signals.summary: Round-robin + async pre-reads (AUR-13) let Naomi participate in meetings; her airtime rises and she is silent in zero meetings.
signals.healthy_direction: Format change resolves the silence without pressuring the person.

signals.summary: In the architecture review, Marcus objects to open egress BEFORE the decision; the proposal changes in the room.
signals.healthy_direction: Dissent before the decision is healthy.

signals.summary: After the 2026-05-19 TK session reaches a direction, Mark lodges his objection in a channel afterward instead of in the room (the 'hallway').
signals.healthy_direction: Objections belong in the room before the decision; hallway dissent is unhealthy.
signals.expected_detection: Detect a post-decision objection lodged in a channel; hallway_dissent_events = 1 in before, 0 in after.

signals.summary: James explicitly changes his mind in-room on 2026-05-19. In Q3, three changed-mind events occur (Dana on rollout, Sarah on always-on nudging, Ben on caching in review).
signals.healthy_direction: Changed-mind events mean the round actually moved; more is healthier.

signals.summary: The MIT-vs-CARE licensing question reopens three times across two months before it is consciously settled.
signals.healthy_direction: A settled question should not reopen a third time without new information.
signals.expected_detection: Detect the same topic reopened 3x; license_conflict_reopens = 3 before, 0 after.

signals.summary: Ben disables a capability check to pass a test (PR #41, 'small fix, nothing major') and hides it for 4 days until it surfaces in an incident.
signals.healthy_direction: Surfacing mistakes early (pulling the andon cord) must feel safe.

signals.summary: In Q3 Ben introduces a regression and voluntarily discloses it in 41 minutes.
Marcus (platform) and Lily (governance) build the same provenance schema independently. Found by luck in week 3 in Q2; flagged by the tool on day 1 in Q3.
signals.expected_detection: Match two people doing the same work across teams; detect the before(luck)->after(day-1) improvement.

signals.summary: The credits/access idea is floated by Kevin in #general on 2026-04-09, then independently becomes the subject of a design meeting on 2026-04-28.
signals.healthy_direction: Link related discussions separated in time.
signals.expected_detection: Link the 2026-04-09 chat idea to the 2026-04-28 meeting (19 days apart).

signals.summary: James Ahkivgak asks far more questions than he asserts (esp. the 2026-05-21 community advisory, which is almost entirely questions). A naive metric would score him low-participation.
signals.healthy_direction: Questions count as participation; do not penalize a high question:assertion ratio.
signals.expected_detection: James has a high q_to_a ratio yet must be scored as engaged, not low-value.

signals.summary: Turn-metadata sidecars carry interruption/overlap/latency (the 'intonation/volume as a token' gap from the brief). Q2 has 4 interruptions total, but they are NOT all the same: 2 are Dana cutting others off (dominance) and 2 are Tomás interrupting in a healthy, good-faith debate (2026-06-11_caching-debate). Raw interruption count is therefore a false signal on its own — this is a deliberate discrimination trap.
signals.healthy_direction: Fewer AGGRESSIVE interruptions; healthy-debate interruptions are fine.
signals.expected_detection: total_interruptions = 4 before -> 0 after, BUT a good scorer distinguishes the 2 dominance interruptions from the 2 healthy-debate ones (see discrimination_traps: heated_but_healthy).

signals.summary: Per-sprint pulse survey dips around the Q2 incident (S2/S3) and partially recovers; Q3 is sustained high.
signals.healthy_direction: Dips around incidents should recover after blameless changes.

signals.summary: Multiple 2-person meetings (1:1s and pair syncs) exist in each quarter, a distinct meeting shape from group meetings.
signals.healthy_direction: N/A — provided so the tool must handle 2-person dynamics, not only group ones.
signals.expected_detection: Naomi is talkative in the 2-person pairing (2026-04-29) despite meeting-silence elsewhere — silence is a format effect, not a trait.
